subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: What Claude CLI auth identity policy should OpenClaw use when the local credential source flips between file and keychain but the selected auth profile appears to represent the same identity-less OAuth login?
rationale: Current source can reproduce the spurious session invalidation, but relaxing the local credential part changes an auth/session boundary and prior related PRs were blocked specifically on whether identity-less Claude CLI credentials can be trusted enough to preserve sessions.

options.title: Approve A Narrow Internal Claude CLI Fix
options.body: Authorize a Claude-CLI-specific policy that suppresses storage-presence churn only when an unchanged selected profile owns the session, with regression tests and fail-closed behavior for logout or unproven identity changes.

options.title: Require Identity-Bearing Host Proof First
options.body: Keep current fail-closed behavior until Claude CLI credentials expose or OpenClaw can safely derive a stable account identity that distinguishes real account switches.

options.title: Defer To User Mitigation
options.body: Leave the issue open but do not change the auth boundary now, and document mitigations such as avoiding mixed Claude CLI/auth-profile rotation setups.

recommendation.title: Approve A Narrow Internal Claude CLI Fix
recommendation.body: Authorize a Claude-CLI-specific policy that suppresses storage-presence churn only when an unchanged selected profile owns the session, with regression tests and fail-closed behavior for logout or unproven identity changes.
